manual.title: The 3x Documentation Scheme
manual.subtitle: A project-neutral system for explaining what, how, and why
manual.description: Use one structured source to create a searchable project manual for people and agents. See the [CLI and format reference](commands.html) for exact commands and fields.
manual.footer: 3x Documentation Scheme {{project.version}} · Adapt the model; keep the reasoning visible.

sections.title: The Core Model
sections.description: The scheme documents observable behavior, implementation, and design intent as one reviewable unit.

entries.title: The three-question contract
entries.summary: Every subject answers What, How, and Why in that order.
entries.what: Provides a repeatable shape for documenting a component, command, workflow, policy, or architectural decision.
how: What defines behavior, inputs, outputs, guarantees, and visible failure modes.
How traces implementation, data flow, dependencies, and operational boundaries.
Why records constraints, trade-offs, intent, and meaningful alternatives.
entries.why: Readers usually need all three perspectives but at different moments. Keeping them adjacent prevents reference material from drifting away from implementation detail or design rationale.

entries.title: Manual structure
entries.summary: Project metadata, presentation settings, sections, and entries remain separate but composable.
entries.what: Organizes a manual into reader-oriented sections containing stable, linkable entries. Each entry can include a summary, synopsis, tags, evidence, and related-entry links in addition to its required triad.

how.lead: The JSON hierarchy is deliberately shallow:
points: Project metadata supplies reusable identity and version values.
Manual metadata describes the document and its badges.
Sections create navigation groups and entries carry the actual explanations.
Theme values alter presentation without changing content.

entries.why: A predictable hierarchy is easy for humans to review, agents to generate, schemas to validate, and renderers to transform without parsing hand-authored HTML.

sections.title: Authoring a Manual
sections.description: Good 3x documentation begins with project discovery and treats uncertainty explicitly.

entries.title: Scope and inventory
entries.summary: Choose subjects by reader need, not merely by source-tree shape.
entries.what: Identifies which capabilities, boundaries, workflows, policies, and decisions deserve entries and which audience the manual serves.
how: Name the primary audience and the decisions they need to make.
Inventory user-visible capabilities and operational workflows.
Map architecture boundaries and consequential design decisions.
Group subjects into a learning path, then assign stable kebab-case IDs.
entries.why: Mirroring folders produces implementation indexes rather than useful manuals. Reader-oriented scope keeps the document navigable and avoids exhaustive but low-value function commentary.

entries.title: Facts, inference, and rationale
entries.summary: Implementation claims require evidence; inferred rationale must be labeled.
entries.what: Separates observed project facts from interpretation so readers can judge confidence and trace important claims.
how: Write What from behavior that can be demonstrated or tested.
Write How from inspected source, configuration, runtime behavior, and operational records.
Write Why from decision records or maintainer statements when available.
When intent is not recorded, say that the rationale is inferred and name the evidence supporting the inference.
entries.why: Plausible explanations are easy to invent and hard to detect later. Explicit provenance prevents a polished manual from becoming an authority for facts the project never established.

entries.title: Evidence and relationships
entries.summary: Entries expose their supporting artifacts and conceptual neighbors.
entries.what: Attaches files, tests, decision records, commands, or URLs to claims and connects entries that readers commonly traverse together.
entries.how: Evidence accepts a path string or a labeled target object. Related entries use stable IDs that the validator checks and the renderer turns into local links.
entries.why: Traceability shortens verification and maintenance. Explicit relationships add useful navigation without forcing the section hierarchy to represent every conceptual connection.

sections.title: Dynamic Adaptation
sections.description: The same content contract supports local writing, automated releases, CI checks, and agent-assisted maintenance.

entries.title: Metadata and runtime overrides
entries.summary: Change shared values once or inject release-specific values during a build.
entries.synopsis: python3 scripts/manual.py build SOURCE --set project.version=2.0.0 --output index.html
entries.what: Resolves metadata placeholders throughout the document and permits scalar values to be overridden from the command line.
how: Place a double-braced path such as `project.name` or `project.version` in textual fields.
The builder resolves placeholders against the source document before validation.
Each `--set PATH=VALUE` assignment updates an existing scalar before resolution.
entries.why: Versions, names, URLs, and theme values recur throughout documentation. Central values and build-time injection prevent repetitive edits and make release automation deterministic.

entries.title: Validation and visible gaps
entries.summary: Incomplete triads fail; weaker traceability remains visible as a warning.
entries.what: Checks required structure, stable IDs, dimension content, recognized placeholder text, evidence shape, and related-entry targets.
entries.how: Structural defects and recognized unfinished-writing markers produce a nonzero exit. Missing evidence and unknown related IDs produce warnings that require judgment without blocking exploratory drafts.
entries.why: A manual should never silently present empty reasoning as complete. Separating errors from warnings preserves a firm minimum contract without pretending every quality concern can be decided mechanically.

entries.title: Portable generation
entries.summary: One validated source becomes one searchable, responsive HTML file.
entries.what: Produces a standalone manual with navigation, full-text filtering, stable anchors, responsive triad cards, evidence disclosure, and print styles.
entries.how: The standard-library generator escapes content, applies a deliberately small inline notation, embeds CSS and JavaScript, and writes a dependency-free HTML document.
entries.why: A single artifact is easy to preview locally, attach to a release, publish on any static host, archive, or inspect in restricted environments.

sections.title: Keeping It Alive
sections.description: The scheme is most useful when documentation evolves with the project rather than following it later.

entries.title: Maintenance lifecycle
entries.summary: Review documentation in the same change that alters documented behavior or rationale.
entries.what: Treats manual source as maintained project material with validation in local workflows and continuous integration.
how: Run `check` in CI for every proposed change.
Use `watch` while restructuring or writing several entries.
Update What when contracts change, How when implementation boundaries move, and Why when constraints or decisions change.
Preserve entry IDs during title edits and review the built artifact before release.
entries.why: Documentation drift is primarily a workflow problem. Co-locating review and enforcing the minimum contract makes stale reasoning easier to catch when relevant context is still available.

entries.title: Agent adaptation workflow
entries.summary: Agents use the same schema, evidence expectations, and validation gate as human authors.
entries.what: Gives coding and documentation agents an explicit protocol for discovering, drafting, checking, and handing off a project manual.
how: Read the schema and the project sources in scope.
Inventory behavior and architecture before drafting entries.
Cite implementation-specific claims and label inferred rationale.
Preserve stable IDs, run validation and generation, then report warnings requiring human judgment.
entries.why: Structured outputs reduce ambiguity between tools and sessions. Using the human workflow also keeps agent-produced documentation reviewable instead of creating a separate, opaque automation path.
